items.item_text: Possession of valid California RN and Advanced Practice license [i.e., Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) or Nurse Practitioner license]
Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Certificate within 3 months of hire (if NP licensed)
National Board Certification, if an NP, in an aligned specialty with the practice area
American Heart Association (AHA) Basic Life Support (BLS) CPR Certification or UC Davis Health CPR
Graduation with a master's degree, DNP or PhD in Nursing from an accredited School of Nursing
One year or greater clinical experience in the care of adult acute care medical surgical patients
Two (2) or more years experience as CNS or NP in the care of adult acute care medical surgical patients
Skills and experience to apply relevant theories and concepts to clinical practice.
Ability to cope with personal stress experienced by team members, other professionals, and caretakers.

Leverages in depth knowledge of one or more clinical specialty areas to effectively manage highly complex inpatient medical surgical care. This includes multidisciplinary collaboration that identifies and prioritizes nursing care needs for a population of inpatient medial surgical patients. Develops, implements and evaluates new models of practice across the continuum of care. Leads the implementation of new policies and procedures across all nursing units. Collaborates with other clinical nurse specialists and health system leadership to lead change and develop evidence-based models of practice.
85% - Professional Practice, Health System Leadership, and Coordination and Collaboration

Mentors excellence in patient care across a diversified patient population. Applies knowledge, experience and judgment to determine the importance of a situation, set priorities, and use abstract thought to evaluate clinical situations. Develops and implements evidence-based patient and staff education. Demonstrates leadership skills. Demonstrates accountability for own practices as defined by the Nurse Practice Act.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Judgement skills to effectively meet the needs of patients.
Self-direction and organizational skills to function in and independent role.
